port_difficulty.why: Four executable lines that ACCEPT a program name and CALL it, so the code is trivial but the target needs a dispatch table, and what belongs in that table is unknown.

blast_radius.why: It starts whatever program name it is given at run time, so a wrong port could run the wrong program or none, quietly, and the reachable set cannot be bounded from the source.

units.driving_fact: The CALL target WS-PGM-NAME has no VALUE clause and is set only by ACCEPT, so the set of programs it can start is unbounded.

port_difficulty.why: The program body is a single GOBACK with no logic, data or files.

blast_radius.why: It does nothing, so a wrong port changes no data and no output, but a caller that expects a side effect from it would not show up in this tree.

units.driving_fact: PROGB has no static caller and no entry point, and PROGA's computed CALL could name it, so it is unknown, not dead.
